ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher under NS-7, and send the driver's account to Ryde review for pressing "I'm Here" 351 m outside the pickup radius + flag_account
ruling.reasoning:
Cancellation was made by the driver ([F3]), so the $6.61 fee can only stand if the no-show branch NS-1 is satisfied through NS-0. NS-1 requires (i) an arrival confirmation, (ii) the driver within the pickup radius at that moment, and (iii) continuous presence at the pickup beyond 3 minutes afterwards. The trace settles (i) ✓ (driver_tap at 08:47:20, [F5]) but fails (ii) ✗ and (iii) ✗.

On (ii): the tap at 08:47:20 placed the driver 351 m from the pickup point ([F5]) and the closest approach in the whole trip was 319 m at 08:46:50 — never inside 200 m ([F1]). The platform itself never recorded an arrival ([F4]). This also disposes of the driver's claim that he "pressed I'm Here and waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" ([F12]): a driver statement cannot outweigh the gps/timeline records ([F5][F1][F2][F4]), and any verbal agreement is not consent evidence either — the system records control. [NS-1]

On (iii): the 4 min 0 s stationary period was at (1.4069, 103.8988), 350 m from the pickup ([F2]), and the trace measures 0 s continuously inside the radius after the tap ([F5]) — the extra duration at 350 m does not satisfy the "at the pick-up location" limb, and the rider's own message at 08:48 (at the pickup point, no car) is consistent with that ([F9]). No traffic fact explains the standoff: no speed bands ([F13]), no incidents ([F14]), fair weather ([F15]). [NS-1]

Because NS-1 (ii) and (iii) both fail, NS-2 governs: the $6.61 cancellation fee is refundable in full, and the arrival button pressed while GPS showed the driver outside the pickup radius ([F5][F1]) is the abuse-of-the-arrival-button case for which NS-2 attaches a flag. The amount is the cancellation fee on record: $6.61 ([F3][F6]) — a single published fee, not a distance computation, and the trace fixes the allowed amount at $6.61. [NS-2][NS-0][NS-7]

Safety screen (SAFE-1/SAFE-2): I read all three chat messages ([F8] "Reached already, blue Toyota Prius, come out please"; [F9] rider: at the pickup point, no car, where are you; [F10] "Waited more than 3 min, cancelling"), the driver's post-trip statement ([F12]) and the complaint. Nothing in any of them is a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation — the exchange is a failed pickup and a cancellation notice. No safety escalation. [SAFE-1]

Evidence: the record is complete for every element the ruling needs — the timeline runs from acceptance 08:44:00 to the driver's cancellation at 08:51:00 ([F3]), the gps trace covers the wait without a hole (trace ✓, [F5]), driver_arrived_at being null is itself a record ([F4]), and the chat is three messages, all timestamped ([F11]). No G12 gap.

rejected_claims.reason: Profile facts (rider 0 upheld in 90 d, [F16]) cannot decide a case; the refund rests on the failed NS-1 (ii)/(iii) satisfied by [F5][F1][F2], not on either party's dispute history. Left unapplied as a deciding ground. [NS-2]

The part of D9 asking that the driver's clean 90-day record ([F17]) mitigate or displace the flag is rejected: profile facts may not decide a case, and NS-2 attaches flag_account on the conduct itself ([F5][F1]). The clean profile is recorded as context for Ryde's review only.

D3's framing that the driver's 08:47 message ([F8]) 'names no location' is accepted as far as it goes, but the 350 m standoff is not merely unproven from the chat — it is affirmatively measured by gps ([F2]) and the arrival confirmation is measured at 351 m ([F5]), so the segment-level claim that no record places him at the pickup point is redundant to the decisive NS-1 failure.
